According to local media reports, Darya Shipilova, a technician employed at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East, died on Oct. […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: The Caspian Sea has been shrinking for decades. Now, a new island has emerged
item.description: Scientists warn that parts of the northern Caspian could face an Aral Sea-like scenario, while climate change and human water use are adding pressure on the region. Fuente: Euronews.

item.title: African park once called a “silent graveyard” now has 37 rhinos and seven calves
item.description: Zinave National Park in Mozambique experienced severe wildlife loss during a 16-year civil war, which impacted biodiversity. Rewilding efforts initiated in 2016 have since introduced several species, including rhinos and lions. The introduction of 250 elephants has helped restore the park's ecosystem and enhance habitats for various species. Conservation programs and anti-poaching strategies have also been implemented to protect newly introduced wildlife. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Hunter Valley community group wins landmark high court climate change case
item.description: Ruling on Mount Pleasant coalmine shows ‘we cannot continue to dig up coal … and pretend the consequences have nothing to do with us’, group says Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast A Hunter Valley community group has won Australia’s first high court case to consider climate change, in a ruling advocates say sets a binding national precedent for fossil fuel projects in New South Wales. In a landmark judgment, the nation’s highest court ruled that the approval of MACH Energy’s Mount Pleasant coalmine expansion in Muswellbrook was invalid. Continue reading... Publicado también por: The Guardian - Environment. Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: New crocodile species found fossilized in stone used to build Egypt’s Great Sphinx
item.description: A new species of extinct crocodile from Egypt has been discovered, sharing more than just its home with the Great Sphinx. Herugavialis cairensis was found in the very same rocks used to build the iconic monument. And, just as the Sphinx is famously missing the tip of its nose, the fossil crocodile is also missing the tip of its snout. Publicado también por: Phys.org. Fuente: Mongabay.
item.dc:creator: Liz Kimbrough

item.title: Lake Hartwell Shoreline Cleanup: Drought exposes long-hidden trash; volunteers pull record 36 tires
item.description: In a remarkable display of community spirit, volunteers have gathered over 8,300 pounds of litter from the shores of Lake Hartwell, driven by an ongoing drought that has unveiled hidden debris. Amid concerns regarding the Clemson Lower Diversion Dam Saddle Dike, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers has enforced specific restrictions. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Newly available satellite data show just how flawed some river models can be
item.description: "Is there enough water? What's happening with climate change? How do I operate my hydro plant? In a world of water problems, there are problems that we need a good model to solve," says Colin Gleason, a hydrologist in the Riccio College of Engineering at the University of Massachusetts Amherst. But the models are only as good as the math that they're based on, and short of measuring every river in the world, there is no way to check this on a global scale. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: AI techniques behind image creation improve flash flood forecasts across U.S. river basins
item.description: A flash flood can devastate a community for years in a matter of minutes. These disasters account for roughly 85% of floods and cause thousands of deaths annually worldwide, with water levels capable of shooting up 30 feet (9 meters) and receding to normal levels in the span of a single, unpredictable day, according to the National Weather Service. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: It looks like the Atlantic storm season may finally produce a hurricane
item.description: To date, this Atlantic tropics year has been exceptionally quiet. Fuente: Ars Technica.

item.title: New Zealand's native plant seeds may survive wildfires
item.description: Mākaka (native broom) and kōwhai seeds might be able to survive the heat of fires, new research shows. Scientists heated native and exotic seeds in a lab oven to temperatures they may face in the soil during a fire, expecting only the exotics—which often experience fires in their homelands—to survive. However, mākaka and kōwhai seeds survived up to 80°C, and mākaka seeds even sprouted in response. Māhoe, tī kōuka (cabbage tree) and matagouri seeds died after heating, while invasive gorse survived 100°C and sprouted. As fires get more common in NZ, it's important to understand if any native… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How AI could help predict and explain water levels in the Great Lakes
item.description: In January 2013, Lake Michigan reached its lowest water level on record. Seven years later, in the summer of 2020, it broke the opposite record with widespread flooding, eroded shorelines and closed lakeside roads. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Indigenous activist Kynan Tegar on Indonesia’s fires, and defending the Earth
item.description: Indigenous activist and filmmaker Kynan Tegar joins the Mongabay Newscast this week to discuss the impacts of the fires devastating Kalimantan, the Indonesian portion of the island of Borneo. Some 48,000 hectares (about 119,000 acres) of land have burned so far this year; Kynan says these fires are intentional on the part of agricultural corporations. […] Fuente: Mongabay.
item.dc:creator: Mikedigirolamo

item.title: Hit songs fade faster from the Billboard charts than albums
item.description: Favorite songs can stay with us for a lifetime, but their shelf life on the music charts is fleetingly short. Tracks that shoot up the U.S. Billboard charts may flood the airwaves for a short while, but just a few weeks later, they have vanished. The outlook for albums is far more enduring, according to a new paper published in the journal Royal Society Open Science. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 100 conservation projects are looking for funding after USAID’s closure
item.description: Founder’s Briefs: An occasional series where Mongabay founder Rhett Ayers Butler shares analysis, perspectives and story summaries. Twenty months after the dismantling of USAID, a new analysis documents what the international development agency’s disappearance has meant for conservation projects around the world. Projects have stalled or collapsed in countries from Kenya to Bangladesh, reports Mongabay’s […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: Oliver Blume, CEO de Volkswagen: "Es el momento de fijar el rumbo correcto sobre el CO₂ y el comercio con China"
item.description: La industria europea del automóvil se acerca a uno de sus años decisivos para definir cómo quiere que sea su mercado en los próximos años. En 2027 se contabilizarán las emisiones medias de los fabricantes y se echarán cuentas. El que se pase, tendrá que pagar. Todo ello mientras los reguladores presionan por el made in Europe y dejan la puerta abierta a los coches chinos con motores de combustión. Por eso Volkswagen ya presiona. "El momento" . "Ahora es el momento de fijar el rumbo correcto para el ‘Made in Europe’, la normativa de CO₂ y el comercio con China". Son las palabras de Oliver… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: Shooting light pulses down a 3-kilometer borehole could illuminate seismic hazards
item.description: A better understanding of how earthquakes occur and what happens during a rupture is important for assessing seismic risk. Small earthquakes, which are more frequent than large ones, are a tempting data set, but they're hard to study, in large part because their energy is quickly sapped as it travels through Earth. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Djokovic ends trophy drought with victory in China
item.description: Novak Djokovic wins the China Open for a seventh time after Alex de Minaur retires in the final in Beijing, as the Serb wins the 102nd title of his career. Fuente: BBC Sport.

item.title: Solar power helps Amazon communities ditch diesel and prepare for El Niño drought
item.description: SANTAREM, Brazil (AP) — Off-grid solar power is spreading across Brazil’s Amazon, helping remote communities prepare for severe drought while replacing costly, polluting diesel generators. In Nova Sociedade, where residents walked up to 20 kilometers for water during the historic 2024 drought, solar panels now power pumps supplying clean water to 36 families. Household systems […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.description: Relics of ancient wet forests stretch across the coast of Queensland state in Australia. In a landscape made patchwork by agriculture, volunteers, community groups and Indigenous rangers in Australia’s Wet Tropics now grow more than 300,000 native plants to turn cleared pasture back into rainforest. As the marine program manager for the nonprofit Redd Fish Restoration Society, she regularly checks on a newly created kelp nursery growing within the traditional territory of […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.description: In October 2006, I was supposed to be starting my dissertation research on tropical reforestation in Indonesia. Instead, I found myself in the forests of Tanjung Puting National Park in Central Kalimantan helping locals to fight fires with brooms, backpack pumps, and hoses connected to hand-dug water wells. item.description: HONG KONG — “Spiderman … Tom Holland,” two secondary school boys repeated to each other as they watched conservationist Harry Wong nimbly climb a tall tree at their school, St. Louis School, in downtown Hong Kong. On a humid September afternoon, Wong installed a nest box for yellow-crested cockatoos (Cacatua sulphurea) on a candlenut tree […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: Veteran conservative lawyer quits Trump’s interior department and warns of ‘assault on the rule of law’
item.description: John Murdock had been working for the agency for 18 years and his resignation comes during an exodus of longtime federal workers and scientists An 18-year veteran of the US Department of the Interior has resigned in protest from the sprawling federal agency, denouncing “a deeply troubling assault on the rule of the law” that took place at the department under Donald Trump. John Murdock, an attorney and self-described conservative Christian, began working for the agency’s legal office in 2002. In his resignation letter, first sent to his supervisor earlier this year and obtained exclusively by… Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.title: As the planet warms, cities like Bangkok could be increasingly inundated by deadly floods
item.description: In the humid tropics of Southeast Asia, afternoon thunderstorms roll through almost every day. Daytime heat causes towering, fluffy cumulonimbus clouds to form and swell before unleashing torrential rain on cities such as Singapore, Hong Kong and Bangkok. In these places, drainage systems are designed to cope with short, heavy downpours. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Rising heat linked to faster telomere loss in wild Australian birds
item.description: Extreme heat can have a profound impact on wild animals, causing their death in the most extreme cases and leaving less visible marks in others. Understanding the effects of temperature changes on specific species could inform conservation efforts and other initiatives aimed at protecting natural ecosystems from climate change. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: From drought to deluge: ‘Super’ El Niño’s expanding reach
item.description: Across Papua New Guinea, water sources are drying up, crops are failing and food prices are rising months before the worst agricultural impacts are expected. Behind those warning signs is an El Niño whose Pacific Ocean temperatures have already surpassed the equivalent measurements during the historic 1997 and 2015 events – part of an unfolding climate pattern being dubbed a “Super El Niño” by some climate watchers. Fuente: UN News.

item.title: El Niño gana fuerza en América Latina: sequía, hambre y riesgo de inundaciones marcan los próximos meses
item.description: El fenómeno de El Niño de 2026-2027 podría convertirse en uno de los más intensos de los que se tiene constancia. En América Latina y el Caribe, unos 41 millones de niños y niñas vivirán entre octubre y diciembre en zonas donde se esperan lluvias muy por encima o por debajo de lo habitual. En partes de Centroamérica, el Caribe y el norte de Sudamérica, sus efectos empiezan a superponerse a una situación ya marcada por pérdidas de cosechas, escasez de agua e inseguridad alimentaria. Fuente: Noticias ONU.

item.title: Seagrass meadows bounce back with new fish communities
item.description: Seagrasses are flowering plants that thrive in marine environments and form extensive meadows along the tropical Queensland coast. New James Cook University research shows the seagrass meadows of Trinity Inlet in Cairns Harbor have recovered after severe cyclones and flooding nearly wiped them out—but with a new mix of fish species. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 16 new fungal species found hiding in Thailand’s flowers
item.description: Researchers surveying garden and wild flowers across northern Thailand have uncovered 16 previously unknown species of black, yeast-like fungi living inside the flowers, according to a recent study. The newly described fungi belong to the Aureobasidium genus, a commonly occurring group of yeast that can be found almost everywhere, from air and human skin, to […] Fuente: Mongabay.
item.dc:creator: Shreya Dasgupta

item.title: Drax datacentre could create nearly twice the yearly emissions of all Gatwick flights
item.description: Exclusive: Campaign group’s analysis of North Yorkshire plans finds datacentre would have to burn 4.9m tonnes of wood a year Drax’s planned datacentre could produce nearly double the emissions of all flights out of Gatwick airport each year by burning 4.9m tonnes of wood annually, an analysis has shown. Campaigners say this would make it “one of the dirtiest datacentres out there”. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.
item.dc:creator: Pippa Neill Environment reporter

item.title: Helping 100,000 amphibians safely cross the road
item.description: Every year, thousands of salamanders and frogs try to cross from their wooded winter homes in the U.S. state of New Hampshire to the swamps they breed in. But the road is a dangerous place — unless you have the help of New Hampshire’s Salamander Brigades. Fuente: Mongabay.
item.dc:creator: Sam Lee

item.title: US households pay 62% more for water than they did a decade ago, study finds
item.description: For-profit water corporations, federal cuts and climate crisis are ‘supercharging water rate hikes’, study co-author says US households are paying 62% more for drinking water than they did a decade ago – outpacing inflation, grocery prices and household incomes, according to a new study. Food & Water Watch, a Washington DC-based non-profit, analyzed 2025 billing data from the 500 largest community water systems in the US, which together serve about 155 million people, or 45% of the country’s population. The analysis compared current rates with data from a similar Food & Water Watch survey… Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.
item.dc:creator: Maya Yang

item.title: Several killed in Senegal as heavy rains cause flooding, damage to infrastructure
item.description: Torrential rainfall and flash flooding left parts of Senegal’s capital Dakar underwater on Monday with other regions of the country also affected. Fuente: Africanews.

item.description: Indonesia’s government is imposing new restrictions on access to geospatial data, raising concerns among researchers and activists that it will suppress environmental science and advocacy work in one of the world’s most biodiverse countries. For around a month, visitors to an interactive mapping platform maintained by the Ministry of Forestry have been greeted with a […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: Global review reveals major blind spots in our understanding of climate change impacts on Mediterranean ecosystems
item.description: A new global review of observed climate change impacts on plant communities reveals major gaps in where and how we monitor some of the world's most climate-vulnerable ecosystems. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Why some Indigenous communities don't resist oil extraction in their territories
item.description: More than half of the Ecuadorian Amazon has been marked for oil drilling, overlapping with Indigenous territories and areas of high biodiversity. The ecological and cultural impacts of oil extraction are well documented and have fueled some of Latin America's most prominent environmental movements. Yet at the local level, extraction is not always met with resistance. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Nepal ends flood search with over 5,000 still missing, including 189 Indians
item.description: Nepal has suspended non-essential search operations after the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli floods that occurred on August 26. The floods resulted in 1,455 deaths, with 5,285 people still unaccounted for, including many foreign tourists. Among the missing individuals are 189 Indians, along with tourists from various other countries. The government has shifted its focus towards reconstruction and rehabilitation efforts rather than continuing search operations. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: Vishant Agarwala

item.title: Nepal calls off disaster rescue activities with 5,285 still missing
item.description: Nepal has ended the search-and-rescue operation for the more than 5,000 people still missing after the devastating August flood. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.description: On June 17, 2015, Philippine officials confiscated thousands of turtles in cement tanks from a warehouse in Palawan, an island province in the Philippines. More than 3,800 of them were endangered Palawan forest turtles (Siebenrockiella leytensis), piled as many as a dozen deep, awaiting export. Some had ulcers on the undersides of their shells or […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: Landmark gorge reopens to visitors after 'huge job' fixing flood damage
item.description: Danggu Geikie Gorge is welcoming its first visitors in more than three years, after the devastating Fitzroy River Floods destroyed almost all its infrastructure. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Long-term logging experiment reveals how protecting the forest floor helps preserve soil carbon
item.description: Forest soils store an estimated 40% of the world's terrestrial carbon, but estimates suggest that around 15–30% of that soil carbon is lost when a forest is harvested. Tracking such losses can be tricky: wildfires, insects, disease and past forest management can all affect forest soil carbon stores, and tree type, climate and harvesting method can all affect how much carbon is lost. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Uncertainty mounts as Suriname struggles to evict illegal settlers in the Amazon
item.description: The government in Suriname this year said it planned to evict illegal settlers in the Amazon Rainforest, and possibly send many of them back to their home countries. But eviction has proven much more complicated than it first appeared, with settlers allegedly ignoring court orders and officials expressing confusion about which people are breaking what […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.description: How the court will lean is unclear amid Suncor Energy and ExxonMobil’s attempt to stop lawsuits at state level The US supreme court began its new nine-month term hearing arguments on Monday in a major case in which big oil companies attempted to strike a fatal blow against lawsuits that seek to hold them accountable for the climate crisis . item.title: La Alhambra lleva más de seis siglos aguantando terremotos. Ahora quiere un plan por escrito para salvar sus Palacios Nazaríes
item.description: El pasado verano se produjo un terremoto de magnitud 5 con epicentro en Alhendín . El evento dio origen a una serie con más de 400 seísmos en pocos días (hoy ya son más de 1.700 ). En aquellos días, la ciudad vivió semanas de incertidumbre y el Patronato cerró la Alcazaba durante más de un mes . Después la reabrió con un recorrido adaptado. Pero una pregunta se formuló pensando en lo que pudiera pasar: ¿y si la Alhambra se derrumbara? Qué ha pasado. Con el susto aún reciente, el Patronato ha empezado a tramitar un plan para proteger los Palacios Nazaríes , el corazón del conjunto. Y no solo… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: Waste plastic yields carbon quantum dots with emissions tunable from UV to yellow-green
item.description: Carbon quantum dots (CQDs) are fluorescent carbon nanomaterials with potential applications in sensing, optoelectronics, displays, anticounterfeiting and environmental technologies. Their optical properties can be adjusted by modifying the carbon structure and surface chemistry, particularly through defect states and the incorporation of heteroatoms. However, achieving predictable and continuous tuning of photoluminescence from a single carbon precursor remains difficult. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Thailand braces for more rain as death toll from recent flooding hits 31
item.description: BANGKOK (AP) — Thai authorities on Monday warned of more rain and flash flooding as the death toll from floods across the country since mid-September rose to 31. item.title: Creíamos que Fukushima estaba encerrada en un sarcófago como Chernóbil. La realidad es mucho más compleja
item.description: Aunque es habitual pensar que Fukushima tuvo la misma solución que Chernóbil y que todo se resolvió con un colosal sarcófago de hormigón, lo cierto es que la realidad es muy diferente y mucho más compleja. Y es que desde que ocurrió el terremoto que después desencadenó el gran tsunami, hace ya quince años, el interior de los reactores es un tema polémico que a día de hoy sigue despertando cierta controversia. Lo que pasó . El 11 de marzo de 2011, Japón sufrió en sus costas orientales un terremoto de magnitud 9.0, como cuenta Business Insider . Esta sacudida tuvo como consecuencia un tsunami… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: Tortoises win support, hyenas face doubts in survey on adding exotic wildlife to UK parks
item.description: Zebras grazing in a UK park might sound like the stuff of a high-budget Hollywood blockbuster, but new research suggests it could one day be vital in the fight against climate change, and that the British public might not mind as much as you'd think. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Frenchwoman buys elephants from abusive owners in Laos
item.description: Once known as "The Land of a Million Elephants", only an estimated 800 elephants remain in Laos, as deforestation and exploitation push the species closer than ever to the brink of extinction. Despite the dwindling numbers, a Frenchwoman has made it her mission to give ageing elephants a new home, buying them from their abusive owners. Our France 2 colleagues report, with FRANCE 24's Andrew Hilliar. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Snakes, bobcats, mountain lions: the secret animal world beneath the Hollywood sign
item.description: An international symbol for the city, the sign is also hallmark of the region’s environmental richness Atop Mount Lee, in the heart of Los Angeles, the wind is quiet. Two red-tailed hawks sail above, barely flapping as they coast the thermal air like surfers on a wave. Standing beside the giant letters of the Hollywood sign, the city seems peaceful. On a clear day, blocks and blocks of homes unfold beneath and the skies reveal sights all the way to Catalina Island – nearly 50 miles out, across the Pacific. That’s the beauty seen from the Hollywood sign. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

The animals were found packed into a car near the boarding area for a Malta-bound catamaran during an inspection at the Sicilian port of Pozzallo, the local unit of Italy’s financial police squad said on Monday. item.title: La ONU impulsa una reforma mundial del tráfico aéreo para reducir retrasos y emisiones
item.description: La Organización de Aviación Civil Internacional reúne esta semana en Montreal a representantes del sector para acelerar una mayor coordinación entre aeropuertos, aerolíneas y controladores. El objetivo es anticipar congestiones antes del despegue, hacer más directas las rutas y reducir tanto el consumo de combustible como las emisiones. Fuente: Noticias ONU.

item.title: Las inundaciones de Madrigueras son extremadamente inquietantes por un motivo: no había ningún río cerca
item.description: El pasado viernes por la tarde, Madrigueras, un pueblo albaceteño de casi 5.000 habitantes , dejó de ser un pueblo para convertirse en un cauce. Las calles se llenaron de agua y barro , los coches empezaron a flotar y a amontonarse y los vecinos se encontraron con una riada donde, sobre el papel, no debería haberla. Ese "sobre el papel" es justo lo que está preocupando a algunas personas: si no hay un cauce fluvial de por medio, ¿qué explica semejante inundación? Los datos. Las inundaciones comenzaron en torno a las 18:00 , cuando se desató la tormenta, y el 112 recibió 108 avisos por casas… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: Food prices rising in Kenya as climate change strains supply

item.title: Antarctica’s 2 native flowering plants responded differently to 7 years of warming
item.description: Research on King George Island examined how two native Antarctic plants responded to long-term warming. Antarctic hairgrass displayed reduced hydraulic conductivity and photosynthesis compared to those in natural conditions. In contrast, Antarctic pearlwort increased both its hydraulic conductivity and photosynthetic capacity. This study provided insights into contrasting adaptive strategies of these plants under sustained environmental changes. These findings highlight the need to understand species-specific responses to climate change effects. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: How farmers are helping reverse farmland wildlife decline
item.description: The resurgence of corn buntings and various wildlife species showcases the power of collaborative conservation work initiated by local farmers. Through the Martin Down and Allenford Farmer Clusters, projects were implemented to improve habitats throughout their farms. This endeavor has led to impressive increases in populations of butterflies and grey partridges over the past ten years. Continued financial investment and diligent monitoring are essential to uphold these successful biodiversity initiatives. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Cataluña enfrenta lluvias e inundaciones récord mientras la alerta se traslada a Girona
item.description: Cataluña afronta las consecuencias de un temporal extraordinario que ha dejado lluvias torrenciales de más de 200 litros por metro cuadrado en algunas zonas, provocando inundaciones, daños en viviendas y afectaciones a negocios. Mientras vecinos evalúan las pérdidas y comienzan las labores de limpieza, las autoridades mantienen la alerta ante el avance del sistema meteorológico hacia el norte de la región. La provincia de Girona, fronteriza con Francia, concentra ahora la mayor preocupación, con avisos de riesgo y llamados a la población para que permanezca a salvo en sus viviendas. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
